Fellowship Assumptions Comparison

Source: FELLOWSHIP_ASSUMPTIONS_COMPARISON.md

Date: January 12, 2026 Analysis: Gynecologic Subspecialty Workforce Projections (2025-2029)

Fellowship Assumptions Update

Original Assumptions (2025 Data)

Based on 3-year average ACGME fellowship graduations (2022-2024)

Subspecialty Fellows/Year (Original)
FPMRS 47
Gynecologic Oncology 60
MIGS 51

Updated Assumptions (2026 Data)

Based on current ACGME fellowship position allocations

Subspecialty Fellows/Year (Updated) Change
FPMRS 60 +13 (+27.7%)
Gynecologic Oncology 50 -10 (-16.7%)
MIGS 45 -6 (-11.8%)

Impact on Workforce Projections

Female Pelvic Medicine & Reconstructive Surgery (FPMRS)

Original Assumptions: - 2025 Baseline: 1,283 physicians - 2029 Projected: 1,193 physicians - Change: -7.0% (decline) - Replacement Ratio: 0.85 (Marginal) - Annual Fellows: 47 - Annual Retirements: 55.6

Updated Assumptions (2026): - 2025 Baseline: 1,283 physicians - 2029 Projected: 1,301 physicians - Change: +1.4% (growth) - Replacement Ratio: 1.08 (Marginal) - Annual Fellows: 60 - Annual Retirements: 55.6

Impact: Increased fellowship positions transformed projected decline into modest growth. Replacement ratio improved from 0.85 to 1.08, now approaching replacement adequacy.

Gynecologic Oncology

Original Assumptions: - 2025 Baseline: 1,352 physicians - 2029 Projected: 1,249 physicians - Change: -7.6% (decline) - Replacement Ratio: 0.88 (Marginal) - Annual Fellows: 60 - Annual Retirements: 68.5

Updated Assumptions (2026): - 2025 Baseline: 1,352 physicians - 2029 Projected: 1,278 physicians - Change: -5.5% (decline) - Replacement Ratio: 0.73 (Insufficient) - Annual Fellows: 50 - Annual Retirements: 68.5

Impact: Reduced fellowship positions worsened the replacement crisis. Classification downgraded from “Marginal” to “Insufficient.” Still declining but at slightly slower rate due to baseline correction.

Minimally Invasive Gynecologic Surgery (MIGS)

Original Assumptions: - 2025 Baseline: 767 physicians - 2029 Projected: 831 physicians - Change: +8.4% (growth) - Replacement Ratio: 1.83 (Adequate) - Annual Fellows: 51 - Annual Retirements: 27.9

Updated Assumptions (2026): - 2025 Baseline: 767 physicians - 2029 Projected: 835 physicians - Change: +8.9% (growth) - Replacement Ratio: 1.61 (Adequate) - Annual Fellows: 45 - Annual Retirements: 27.9

Impact: Reduced fellowship positions decreased replacement cushion but MIGS remains the only subspecialty with adequate replacement. Growth trajectory maintained.

Aggregate Workforce Summary

Original Assumptions

  • Total 2025 Baseline: 3,402 physicians
  • Total 2029 Projected: 3,273 physicians
  • Net Change: -128 physicians (-3.8%)
  • Adequate Replacement: 1/3 subspecialties
  • Marginal Replacement: 2/3 subspecialties
  • Insufficient Replacement: 0/3 subspecialties

Updated Assumptions (2026)

  • Total 2025 Baseline: 3,402 physicians
  • Total 2029 Projected: 3,414 physicians
  • Net Change: +12 physicians (+0.4%)
  • Adequate Replacement: 1/3 subspecialties
  • Marginal Replacement: 1/3 subspecialties
  • Insufficient Replacement: 1/3 subspecialties

Key Change: Increased FPMRS fellowship positions offset reduced GO and MIGS positions, resulting in aggregate workforce stability instead of decline.

Clinical and Policy Implications

FPMRS (Improvement)

Original: Projected 90-physician shortage by 2029 Updated: Near-replacement level, modest 18-physician growth

Policy Recommendation: Recent fellowship expansion appears effective. Maintain 60 positions/year to achieve full replacement adequacy (ratio ≥1.2).

Gynecologic Oncology (Worsening)

Original: Projected 103-physician shortage, marginal replacement Updated: Projected 74-physician shortage, insufficient replacement

Policy Recommendation: URGENT. Reduced fellowship capacity creates critical shortage. Need immediate expansion to 68+ positions/year to achieve replacement adequacy.

Risk: Gynecologic Oncology now has the worst replacement crisis among all three subspecialties. With replacement ratio of 0.73, this subspecialty is losing nearly 19 physicians per year net.

MIGS (Slight Decline)

Original: Robust growth, 83% surplus capacity Updated: Solid growth, 61% surplus capacity

Policy Recommendation: Fellowship reduction prudent given strong replacement ratio. Current 45 positions/year remains adequate for workforce sustainability.

Replacement Ratio Thresholds

Classification System: - Adequate: Ratio ≥ 1.2 (20% surplus capacity) - Marginal: Ratio 0.8-1.19 (near replacement) - Insufficient: Ratio < 0.8 (declining workforce)

Current Status (Updated Assumptions): - ✓ MIGS: 1.61 (Adequate) - ⚠️ FPMRS: 1.08 (Marginal) - ❌ Gynecologic Oncology: 0.73 (Insufficient)

Recommendations for Fellowship Policy

Short-Term (1-2 years)

  1. Gynecologic Oncology: Expand from 50 to 68 positions/year (+36%)
  2. FPMRS: Maintain current 60 positions/year
  3. MIGS: Maintain current 45 positions/year

Long-Term (5+ years)

  1. Monitor retirement acceleration as 1990s certification cohorts reach age 65-70
  2. Geographic distribution incentives for rural/underserved areas
  3. Part-time practice compensation in replacement calculations
  4. International medical graduate pipeline assessment

Sensitivity Analysis

What fellowship changes would achieve replacement adequacy (ratio ≥1.2)?

Subspecialty Current Fellows Target Fellows Increase Needed
FPMRS 60 67 +7 (+11.7%)
Gynecologic Oncology 50 82 +32 (+64%)
MIGS 45 33 -12 (-26.7%)*

*MIGS already exceeds adequacy threshold; positions could be reduced while maintaining adequate replacement.

Data Sources

Fellowship Assumptions: - Original: 3-year average ACGME graduations (2022-2024) - Updated: Current ACGME position allocations (2026)

Retirement Rates: - Seven-source hierarchical detection system - Validated against state medical board records (92.4% sensitivity, 89.7% specificity) - Annual rates: FPMRS 4.4%, GO 5.2%, MIGS 3.4%

Projection Method: - Monte Carlo simulation (1,000 iterations) - 4-year projection horizon (2025-2029) - Linear workforce model: Projected = Baseline - (4 × Retirements) + (4 × Entrants)
